policy: Built-in schedules ship with Meiva. Product schedules (adversarial evaluation, self-evolution, memory) are created enabled by default; cluster-operator schedules are created but disabled. provision_builtin_schedules() (schedule-manager start + `meiva schedules provision`) creates missing built-ins keyed by name and resyncs the script/command of existing ones to the template here; their enabled state and description are never modified.

builtin_schedules.name: c9-daily-report
builtin_schedules.description: Daily CI-minute reconciliation at 05:00 cluster time — appends the trailing 24h of CI runs to the attribution ledger (idempotent by run id) and emits the ci_usage_daily event; failures wake the Meiva P0 lead.

builtin_schedules.name: debt-sweep-daily
builtin_schedules.description: Daily 06:30 cluster-time mechanical scan plus one debt-clearing pass landing as the sweeper's chore(sweeper) PR; failures wake the P0 lead.

builtin_schedules.name: adversarial-eval-weekly
builtin_schedules.description: Weekly adversarial probe batch — rotates 5 of 9 behavior-probe cases through fresh eval-isolated agents every Wednesday 04:00 cluster time; quiet on success, wakes an owner agent for human review on any 0-score.

builtin_schedules.name: memory-arbiter
builtin_schedules.description: Memory pool daily maintenance — 4AM consolidation (commit + push + PR merge) and 7AM health check (OKF, size, dedup, stale).

builtin_schedules.name: self-evolution-daily
builtin_schedules.description: Daily incremental self-evolution scan — runs daily_scan.py at 00:00 (embedded timezone), wakes the self-evolution agent on ALERT (exit 2) or timeout.

builtin_schedules.name: self-evolution-weekly
builtin_schedules.description: Weekly self-evolution — fires the self-evolution agent when the past week's event volume clears a minimum threshold (dynamic; busy weeks get a mid-week follow-up).

builtin_schedules.name: model-update-tracker
builtin_schedules.description: Daily upstream model detection — pulls each provider's official model list, diffs the registry, and wakes the P0 lead agent on new candidates (06:00 Asia/Shanghai).

builtin_schedules.name: dev-ci-metrics
builtin_schedules.description: Daily GitHub Actions run-observability collection at 06:20 cluster time — publishes absolute Dev/CI workflow, failure, per-PR, and white-run gauges; failures wake the Meiva P0 lead.

builtin_schedules.name: trace-ship-tempo
builtin_schedules.description: Every five minutes, ship the local OTel trace mirror to the local Tempo viewer: incremental by a per-file watermark so a run sends only new lines, idempotent by span id so a missed window is caught up on the next run, and best-effort so an unreachable viewer never ends the schedule.

builtin_schedules.name: db-write-stall-watch
builtin_schedules.description: Operator sentinel for a stalled database write path (#5310): reads pgBouncer's per-minute stats line from $MEIVA_HOME/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.log and wakes the cluster operator after three consecutive minutes under 20 xacts/s with an average query time above 300 ms. Thresholds come from 29 days of history (40,375 minutes), where the rule marked only the two real incidents; an agent-host crash wave is the consequence it precedes, not the signal.

builtin_schedules.name: sched-dry-import-weekly
builtin_schedules.description: Operator sentinel for the schedules themselves: every Monday 09:00 cluster time it syntax-checks and imports-only executes every stored schedule script in the runner's venv, stopped rows included, then wakes the cluster operator with the exact module or syntax error of each red. It catches the drift class that broke seven in-store scripts in one wave (2026-10-25): the repository moves a module and the database-embedded copies do not roll. `--once` runs a sweep now; `--check-file` is the falsification control.

builtin_schedules.name: log-cred-mask-monthly
builtin_schedules.description: Operator sweep for credentials left in logs: on the 15th at 10:00 cluster time it runs the host-local log-credential scanner (fresh strict scan, same-length masking, strict recount, final dry run) and wakes the cluster operator only when the sweep exits nonzero. The scanner is an operator tool that lives under the runtime home of the machine that owns the schedule manager; on a host without it the run reports rc=2 naming the missing path instead of retrying silently.

builtin_schedules.name: qa-keepalive
builtin_schedules.description: Operator sentinel for one agent's page and inbound watcher on a remote host: the gateway-hosted runner probes an HTTP health URL and a remote process every ten minutes, wakes the owning agent only after two consecutive failed rounds (one bad round is a rollout), then holds a one-hour cool-down and clears the streak on the first healthy round. Ships disabled: the health URL, the probed hosts and the owner are site values in the template.

builtin_schedules.name: agent-watch
builtin_schedules.description: Operator sentinel for duties that stop taking their rounds (#5594): every ten minutes it reads, for each agent with a watching duty, the live session count, the age of the last real turn, and whether a schedule that agent owns still fires on its own cadence, then wakes the agent, tells the lead, or escalates to the user along one ladder -- for an hourly duty: detect at 90 minutes, report to the lead at 180, escalate at 240, with every rung moving out with a longer cadence and the interval between repeats widening as the silence outlasts each rung. A declared heartbeat pause is not silence, and only the turn-age condition treats it as rest: a fleet of dead sessions is still a loss. A signal the host cannot read is reported as blind and never counted as healthy, and a terminated agent is finished rather than silent, so the sentinel never resurrects a duty the user ended.
